findings.asked: Length of an arc from its angle.
findings.wentWrong: Many knew the circumference but then divided it by 260 or misused the 100 degree angle; area-based attempts were common; only the best got all three marks.

findings.asked: Length of the major arc drawn on the diagram.
findings.wentWrong: Most found the minor arc (6.1 cm) instead of the major arc (15.9 cm); some forgot to round to 1 d.p.; weaker candidates used area.
findings.rule: Check which arc is drawn: the major arc uses 360 minus the given angle.

findings.wentWrong: Two out of three was typical: the diameter was not added to the arc; a few found the area or used a wrong circumference formula.
findings.rule: Perimeter of a semicircle = half circumference + diameter.

findings.wentWrong: The perimeter formula was chosen correctly but most halved the circumference and stopped.
findings.rule: Perimeter includes every edge, straight ones too.

ruleToRemember: Arc = angle/360 x 2 pi r; sector area = angle/360 x pi r squared; perimeters include the straight edges; check whether the major or minor arc is wanted.
aStarSignal: Working with the major arc or a reflex angle and combining an arc with straight edges in a perimeter.
